purpose: Prototype v6n: the sensitivity of the reference, asked for by the pre-review of outline v10 for the Journal of Writing Research (round 4) and decided by the researcher (decision 23 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe; decisions 1-3 of .steering/20261108-v6n-reference-sensitivity). (1) A reference built from means, R_mean: R_loc's four medians replaced by means, the rest unchanged, counted on v6m's dose rows with a 75% step added: is 'the positive control is reached only by the largest operations' (v6m part 2) a property of the procedure or of a reference built from medians (round 4: R1 M1, M3, R3 1, editor A; Codex 3: three steps do not fix a boundary)? (2) The direction at the level of the group at every step (v6m part 4's count), beside count 1, a judgement per person (round 4: R2 2, R1 M2). (3) The split-half reliability of the features on v6m's persons (v6l's permutation splits), beside v6l's values on v6k's persons (round 4: R3 4, R3 5).
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-08 after seeing the records and notes of v6k, v6l and v6m (results/prototype_v6k/, results/prototype_v6l/, results/prototype_v6m/) and the pre-review of outline v10 (round 4). The persons are v6m's, whose v6m values have been seen. No value of R_mean, of a 75% row, or of a split-half reliability on v6m's persons has been computed for any person. A first draft was sent to Codex (codex-consult, the conditions text and earlier aggregate results only, no data; .steering/20261108-v6n-reference-sensitivity/codex-consult-output.md) and changed after its seven points (decision 4 of that folder): the scale and the medians of change and base are stated and reported; the readings separate the reach from the difference between references, are narrowed (no mechanism, no equivalence from an interval including 0) and say that the intervals do not include the choice of R_mean; the persons of each comparison are stated; the plans' partners and the positions changed are stated and tallied; the reliability's order of handling is stated; only the listed features are called fixed by construction.
status: Description (status d) throughout: v6m's persons, whose v6m values have been seen, and a reference chosen after v6m's result. The readings below are fixed before any value of the new quantities is seen, so that the description cannot be shaped by them; they are not a confirmation. No rule and no label.

sources.v6m: works/conditions/prototype_v6m.json and results/prototype_v6m/record.json (SHA-256 in earlier): the persons, rows, dose plans, count 1, the rule persons, the paired difference with R_loc, part 2 and part 4.
sources.v6l: works/conditions/prototype_v6l.json and results/prototype_v6l/record.json: R_loc and the split-half reliability (Parsons, Kruijt & Fox 2019, as quoted there).
sources.v6m_notes: results/prototype_v6m/notes.md, verbatim: 'R_loc sees it less, because its six numbers are medians and a share at sentence and subsentence starts, and moving a few long gaps leaves the medians of the many short sentence-initial gaps.' That sentence was written after the run and was not tested; part 1 tests it in the sense below.

data: as v6m (files and SHA-256 in v6's and v6e's conditions).

participants.persons: v6m's: KUPA from position 656 of v6's draw order, the first 200 eligible under v6b's rule; LWP from position 411 of v6e's, the first 200 eligible under v6e's rule (v6m's draw, reused). The run checks that the SHA-256 of each sorted id list and the numbers of ids looked at equal v6m's record.
participants.count_1_persons: v6m's count 1 persons per dataset and task (KUPA essay 175, KUPA copy 200, LWP 197 in v6m's record; checked).

units_parts: as v6m: sentences (counting 'before'), parts odd/even and halves, one threshold 2000 ms.

stages.reused: every stage of v6m (S0, S1, U@2000, U_med, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I, R, R_loc, R_lag, B_complete@2000, Bsd_complete@2000), v6m's code imported.
stages.R_mean: 6 numbers per part, on the gaps the part holds (the gaps R uses, v6b.loc): the mean of ln gap over the gaps labelled sentence, subsentence, word and within (four means); sentence mean minus within mean; the share of long time at sentence and subsentence starts at 2 s (R_loc's sixth number, unchanged). R_mean differs from R_loc only in mean for median in the first five numbers. A part has R_mean exactly when it has R_loc, and so exactly when it has R (v6l: R_loc exists exactly when R does; all need a gap of each of the four labels; checked per person and part), and R_mean's sixth number equals R_loc's (checked). So R, R_loc and R_mean have the same persons in every cell, and the gate 0 persons of R_mean and R_loc are the same set (checked; the persons of every cell and of every paired difference are reported). The fifth number is made from the first and fourth, as in R_loc, so the sentence and within-word parts weigh twice in the distance in both references alike. Index 12.
stages.why_this_reference: chosen after v6m (decision 1 of the folder): to change one thing of R_loc. It is not chosen to be a better reference in general; a mean of ln gaps moves with a few long gaps more than a median does, and so is expected to be more sensitive to cross. It is a second reference beside R_loc, not a replacement, and it has no rule.

rows.reused: v6m's rows with v6m's operations, plans and keys (text/before, text/after, text/none, inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before, random_half, inside_25, inside_50, inside_100, cross_25, cross_50, cross_100).
rows.step_75: inside_75 and cross_75: the same per-person plans as v6m (inside_plan, cross_plan, unchanged), applying the swaps of the first ceil(0.75 m) candidates or givers (a giver without a partner stays). So, per person, inside_25 ⊆ inside_50 ⊆ inside_75 ⊆ inside_100 (swaps and changed positions), and the same for cross; inside_25, inside_50, inside_100 and the cross rows of v6m are unchanged (checked against v6m's record). The plans assign every partner once for all steps (v6m): inside swaps one pair per sentence, cross takes each pool gap at most once, so no gap position is in two swaps of a plan (checked per person) and a later swap cannot undo an earlier one.
rows.row_index: v6m's, then inside_75 14 and cross_75 15 (13 is v6m's contrast in part 4, not used here).
rows.tallies: as v6m, for the eight dose rows: what moved per step (candidates m, swaps made, share swapped, time moved, swaps crossing a part's boundary, givers without a partner, persons with m = 0), and, new, the number of gap positions changed against the text. 'same_as_next_step' compares a step with the next one in v6n's order (25-50, 50-75, 75-100); v6m's step 50 compared with 100, so that tally is not checked against v6m for step 50.

count_1.how: v6m's count 1 (v6b.one; share of persons whose change exceeds the distance between their own two parts, ties 1/2, 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples; each feature scaled by its standard deviation over the cell's persons and the text's two parts, the same scale for the text and the row, fixed across resamples) for KUPA essay and LWP, both baselines, every row (v6m's and the two 75% rows) and every stage (v6m's and R_mean), on all persons with the stage (gate 0); and on rule persons (the stage and R both present, as v6m) for U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I, U_med, B_complete@2000 and Bsd_complete@2000 in the main rows and the eight dose rows, with R, R_loc, R_lag and R_mean counted on those persons.
count_1.keys: v6m's: numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 95, dataset, task, stage, row index, baseline, 0, gate]), R_mean's stage index 12, the 75% rows' indices 14 and 15; gate 0 on all persons, 1 + the stage index of the rule stage for its rule persons (the same for its R, R_loc, R_lag and R_mean). So every cell counted by v6m is reproduced exactly with v6m's keys (checked), and the new cells have keys of their own.
count_1.paired: for each rule stage and dose row: the paired difference of the per-person contributions of the stage and R_loc (v6m's, over the stage's resamples) and, new, of the stage and R_mean (the same persons and resamples). Beside every share, v6b.one's medians of the change and of the own distance (base) and of their ratio, so that a difference between R_mean and R_loc can be read as a larger change, a smaller base or both. For R_mean itself: R_mean - R_loc on the persons with R (gate 0; R_mean's resamples, key gate 0) and on each rule stage's rule persons (that stage's resamples).

part_1_reference_doses.cells: KUPA essay and LWP; odd/even and halves; families inside_p and cross_p; steps 25, 50, 75, 100: 32 cells per stage.
part_1_reference_doses.reported: per cell: R_mean and R_loc on the persons with R (gate 0), each with share, interval and class (above, below, undecided against 0.60), and the paired difference R_mean - R_loc with its interval; per family, set and baseline, the first of the four steps at which each reads above 0.60 ('none' if none does) and whether the share rises with the step (25 <= 50 <= 75 <= 100); the same on the rule persons of each rule stage; for U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000 and I, their class at every step (75 added) and the paired differences with R_loc and with R_mean. Cells fixed by construction (inside_p for U@2000, U_med and B@2000; v6m's) are named and not read. Beside each step, what moved (rows.tallies). Beside the dose rows, R_mean in v6m's main rows (inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before) on the rule persons, with R_loc.
part_1_reference_doses.reading: descriptive, fixed before running; two axes read separately: the reach (each reference's class against 0.60) and the difference between the references (the paired interval). (a) Where R_mean reads a step above 0.60 at which R_loc does not, and the paired interval lies above 0: on these persons, operations and distance, changing the reference from medians to means changes the reach at that step, so 'reached only by the largest operations' is a statement about R_loc and cannot be written as a property of the procedure. It is not read as the mechanism (that the medians ignored the long gaps) nor as R_mean being the better reference. (b) Where R_mean, like R_loc, reads no step below 100 above 0.60 (or none at all): changing the reference to means does not change the reach at these steps; this does not show that the medians play no part (a difference can exist below 0.60; see the paired interval), nor that the reach is the procedure's, since another reference could reach further. (c) A paired interval that includes 0 does not show the two references equal; a paired interval that excludes 0 is reported whatever the classes. (d) A summary below 0.60 where R_mean reads above shows the move less than R_mean does only if its paired interval with R_mean lies below 0. The intervals are conditional on the reference chosen; they do not include the choice of R_mean after v6m's result. 'The first step above' is a statement about these four steps on one random plan per person, and depends on the intervals' bootstrap; it is not an amount needed and not a detection boundary. The steps are shares of each person's eligible sentences or long sentence-initial gaps, not amounts of time. Nothing here changes v6k's or v6m's labels: R_mean is not a gate of any rule.

part_2_group_direction.what: v6m's part 4 count (per person, on the whole-record vector, the signed change row - text per feature; the number of persons and the shares with a change above 1e-9, below -1e-9 and between (every feature here is a log time, a mean of log times, a share, a correlation, a count of presses or seconds, so 1e-9 is far below its resolution and catches only exact zeros and rounding; v6m); the median over persons with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples, key numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 97, dataset, task, stage index, row index, feature index])) for the eight dose rows, KUPA essay and LWP, stages U@2000 (4), B@2000, Bsd@2000, I (3), R_loc (6), R_lag, B_complete@2000 and R_mean (6). The cells counted by v6m (its six dose rows, its stages) are reproduced exactly (checked).
part_2_group_direction.beside: per stage and step, beside each feature's shares of signs: the stage's count 1 share at that step under both baselines (gate 0 and rule persons), so that a direction over persons and a judgement per person against their own parts are read side by side.
part_2_group_direction.fixed: the whole-record B@2000 and I's first number do not change under any row that keeps the record's multiset of gaps (every row here: a whole record is one run, and the mean of the gaps over 200 ms is fixed). v6m's notes found this after its run; here it is stated before, checked per person (|change| <= 1e-9, a violation stops the run), and those two features are reported as fixed and not read. Under inside_p, U@2000's four numbers do not change (each sentence keeps its multiset; v6m), reported as fixed and not read.
part_2_group_direction.reading: descriptive: the direction at the level of the group is read from the shares of the signs (for example 'the change was negative in 97% of persons'); a median whose interval excludes 0 is reported beside, not as consistency across persons and not as a test. Only the features listed under 'fixed' are called fixed by construction. No other direction is called necessary: inside moves short sentence-initial gaps as well as long ones, so even a sentence-start number need not fall in every person; a direction that was anticipated is reported as observed. A consistent direction says that the feature responds to the move on average over persons, not that the summary is usable for a comparison. A share of signs and a count 1 share answer different questions (a direction over persons against a change beyond the person's own variation) and are reported together, neither read as the other.

part_3_reliability.what: v6l's split-half reliability (v6l.reliability, unchanged but for the key) per dataset and task on v6m's count 1 persons (KUPA essay, KUPA copy, LWP), of the text (text/before, counting 'before'): for every feature of S0 (7), U@2000 (4), B@2000 (1), Bsd@2000 (1), B_complete@2000 (1), Bsd_complete@2000 (1), I (3), R (7: R_loc's six and R_lag) and R_mean (6).
part_3_reliability.splits: as v6l: 5000 random splits; in split s a person's n sentences are permuted by one generator per person, numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 98, dataset, task, place]) (place: v6m's index of the id in the sorted ids), drawing its permutations in the order s = 0..4999; the first floor(n / 2) form part A. (v6l's key started with 93; 98 keeps the new persons' draws apart.) The fixed parts odd/even and halves are reported beside (one split each), with v6l's statistics.
part_3_reliability.estimate: as v6l: per feature and split, on the persons with the stage in both parts (at least 10), r_s and rSB_s = 2 r_s / (1 + r_s); the mean and 2.5%/97.5% percentiles over splits with a value; the splits without (by reason); persons per split. As v6l, in this order: a non-finite feature value stops the run; a split with fewer than 10 persons, a feature constant on one side over those persons, or r_s = -1 has no value and is counted by reason; negative r_s are kept. R_loc's and R_mean's features have the same persons in every split (same existence), so they are compared on common persons. The percentile range over splits is the spread over splits, not an interval over the sampling of persons. A feature's mean rSB below 0.50 is named 'low' (v6l).
part_3_reliability.beside: per feature, v6l's mean rSB and interval on v6k's persons (from v6l's record), and the difference new minus v6l. R_mean's features have no v6l value.
part_3_reliability.reading: descriptive, as v6l: a low reliability means that the parts' values of a feature do not order persons alike; it can come from noise within persons or from small differences between persons, and it is not a measure of count 1's baseline (a Euclidean distance over scaled features within a person). The reliability of the values at each boundary (R_loc's and R_mean's four numbers, I's word and within means) is the reliability of the values that recommendation (ii) of the paper would report. A difference between v6m's and v6k's persons is a description of two draws, not a test. Random splits mix sentences from anywhere in the session and are closer in phase than halves (v6l).

checks.reuse: before any new quantity is reported, and stopping the run otherwise: the persons' id SHA-256 and the numbers looked at equal v6m's; v6m's count 1 persons per set; every count 1 cell of v6m's record (gate 0, every row and stage of v6m, both baselines, KUPA essay and LWP) and every rule-person cell of v6m (stage, R, R_loc, R_lag, and paired_minus_R_loc) equal v6m's (persons, share_vs_own and its interval, the paired difference and its interval); v6m's part 4 cells for its rows and stages equal v6m's; v6m's dose tallies for its six rows equal v6m's (but same_as_next_step at step 50); v6m's part 2 summary (classes, first step above among 25, 50, 100, rising) is recomputed from these cells and equals v6m's.
checks.reliability_reuse: on v6k's persons (KUPA essay, KUPA copy, LWP; v6k's draw checked against v6k's record as in v6m), the fixed-part statistics (odd/even and halves: r, rSB, persons, mean and absolute differences, standard deviations) of every feature of v6l's stages equal v6l's record. (The random splits use a new key and are not compared; the splits' code is v6l's, with v6l's check against the count 1 part vectors on the first splits.)
checks.rows: per person: every row's gaps are a permutation of the text's; the four steps are nested (the swaps applied a prefix of the next step's, the changed positions nested); inside_100 equals inside/before.
checks.construction: v6m's identities (B@2000 under the rows and baselines that keep each run's multiset; U@2000, U_med and S1 under inside/before and every inside step; I's first number under all of them), with inside_75; R_mean exists exactly when R_loc does and its sixth number equals R_loc's; the whole-record identities of part_2_group_direction.fixed.
checks.missing: as v6m: a count over fewer than 2 persons is too_few_persons and not read; a summary over fewer than 5 values is not written; a non-finite value stops the run.

prediction: Claude's, written before running. P1: R_mean reads cross_100 above 0.60 in at least 2 of its 4 cells (KUPA essay and LWP, two baselines; persons with R). P2: in LWP, R_mean's first step above 0.60 for inside is 75 or earlier under both baselines. P3: in KUPA essay, R_mean reads inside_100 above 0.60 under both baselines. P4: no rule stage (U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I) reads inside_75 or cross_75 above 0.60 on its rule persons. P5: R_loc in LWP reads inside_75 below or undecided under both baselines. P6: the mean rSB of R_mean's sentence-start mean is lower than that of R_loc's sentence-start median in KUPA essay and in LWP. P7: on v6m's persons every feature of v6l's stages has a mean rSB within 0.15 of v6l's. No value of v6n has been seen.
main_cells: fixed before running, shown first: part 1's table of classes per step for R_loc and R_mean (persons with R) with the paired difference, per family, set and baseline, and the first step above of each; the rule stages' classes at 75; part 2's shares of signs per step for R_loc's and R_mean's first and fifth numbers and I's three, beside count 1; part 3's mean rSB for R_loc, R_mean, B@2000 and I beside v6l's; then the rest in the order of this file.

record.public: results/prototype_v6n/record.json: counts and summaries over persons and the provenance; no press time, gap, key, text, per-person vector, value, change or id (ids only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list); a summary over fewer than 5 values is not written. The data are not redistributed.
record.provenance: git commit and dirty state of the conditions, code and lock; SHA-256 of the conditions, the earlier conditions and records, the code and the data; versions.

limits_written_before: The persons are v6m's, whose v6m values were seen, and R_mean was chosen after v6m's dose result, to be sensitive where R_loc was not: nothing here is a confirmation, and R_mean reading a step is not evidence that the procedure detects that amount of change in general. A trimmed mean or other robust version of the reference, which would show how far R_mean depends on a few long gaps, is not counted: it would be one more reference chosen after the result (decision 4 of the folder). Two references do not bound what a reference could see; a reference built to move with a given operation will see it, so the reading is about these two references. The steps are four on one random plan per person, nested, shares of eligible sentences or gaps, not of time; cells of a family are not independent. inside_p moves short gaps as well as long ones; cross_p moves long gaps out of sentence starts and into other sentences, so means at sentence and word starts move together. Part 2's directions are of whole records in raw units, many correlated features, no correction, and several follow from the definitions. Part 3's reliabilities are of single features over persons, not of count 1's baseline; v6m's and v6k's persons are two draws of the same corpora. Only the 2 s threshold. A share shows sensitivity of a summary to a difference in press times; it says nothing about the cognitive meaning of a pause or the quality of a text.
rerun_rule: as v6k: if a defect of the code is found after the first run, the first record is kept unchanged, the fix and the reason are committed, and the rerun is reported separately beside the first.
generator: as v6k (checked by v6k's code against v6k's conditions).
